It began on March 5 and ended on December 3, followed by [[J. League promotion/relegation series]] matches on December 7 and 10. == General == === Promotion and relegation === * At the end of the [[2004 J.League Division 2|2004 season]], [[Kawasaki Frontale]] and [[RB Omiya Ardija|Omiya Ardija]] were promoted to J1. * At the end of the [[2004 J.League Division 1|2004 season]], there were no relegation to J2. * At the end of the [[2004 Japan Football League|2004 season]], [[Tokushima Vortis]] and [[Thespa Gunma|Thespakusatsu Gunma]] were promoted to J2 from JFL. === Changes in competition formats === * The Division 1 was expanded to 18 clubs, and Division 2 stays at 12 clubs. * The format of Division 1 was changed from the [[Apertura and Clausura|double-season format]] to a single season. * In games that require [[extra time]] in case of a tie (i.e. league cup finals), [[golden goal]] rules were eliminated. Clubs now had to play the full extra time. === Changes in clubs === * JEF United relocates from [[Ichihara, Chiba|Ichihara]] to the prefecture capital, [[Chiba (city)|Chiba]], and becomes [[JEF United Chiba|JEF United Ichihara Chiba]]. == Honours == {| class="wikitable" |- !Competition !Champion !Runner-up !3rd place |- |[[J1 League|J.League Division 1]] |[[Gamba Osaka]] |[[Urawa Red Diamonds]] |[[Kashima Antlers]] |- |[[J2 League|J.League Division 2]] |[[Kyoto Sanga FC|Kyoto Purple Sanga]] |[[Avispa Fukuoka]] |[[Ventforet Kofu]] |- |[[Emperor's Cup]] |[[Urawa Red Diamonds]] |[[Shimizu S-Pulse]] |[[Cerezo Osaka]]

{{flagicon|South Korea}} ''[[Ahn Jung-hwan]]'' |} == Format == Eighteen clubs will play in double round-robin (home and away) format, a total of 34 games each. A club receives 3 points for a win, 1 point for a tie, and 0 points for a loss. The clubs are ranked by points, and tie breakers are, in the following order: * Goal differential * Goals scored * Head-to-head results A draw would be conducted, if necessary. However, if two clubs are tied at the first place, both clubs will be declared as the champions. The bottom two clubs will be relegated to J2, while the 16th placed club plays a two-legged [[J.League Promotion / relegation Series|Promotion/relegation Series]]. ;Changes from previous year * Number of clubs competing increased from 16 to 18 * The season format was changed from the [[Apertura and Clausura|double-season format]] to a single season. * Number of games per club increased from 30 games to 34 games per season. == Table == {{#invoke:sports table|main|style=WDL |show_limit=5 |res_col_header=QR |team1=GAM|name_GAM=[[Gamba Osaka]] |team2=RED|name_RED=[[Urawa Red Diamonds]] |team3=ANT|name_ANT=[[Kashima Antlers]] |team4=JEF|name_JEF=[[JEF United Chiba|JEF United Ichihara Chiba]] |team5=CER|name_CER=[[Cerezo Osaka]] |team6=JÚB|name_JÚB=[[Júbilo Iwata]] |team7=SFR|name_SFR=[[Sanfrecce Hiroshima]] |team8=FRO|name_FRO=[[Kawasaki Frontale]] |team9=FMA|name_FMA=[[Yokohama F.
